chapters.title: Handwritten Machine Learning Notes
chapters.description: Six expanded handwritten guides with small datasets, complete calculations, original page scans, and downloadable PDFs.

chapters.title: MLE, MAP, and Bayesian Prediction
chapters.description: Follow five coin tosses through likelihood, a Beta prior, MAP estimation, and posterior prediction.
chapters.alt: Original handwritten page showing a Beta prior, Bayes rule, posterior exponents and the MAP estimator.
chapters.caption: MLE.pdf, page 3: the prior-to-posterior calculation. The worked coin example above separates the posterior mode from the posterior predictive mean.

chapters.title: Linear Regression: From Gaussian Noise to Ridge and Lasso
chapters.description: Fit three visible rows, derive squared error from Gaussian likelihood, and connect MAP estimation to ridge and lasso regularization.
chapters.alt: Original handwritten page introducing residuals, linear predictions and independent Gaussian observation noise.
chapters.caption: Linear Regression.pdf, page 1: the residual and Gaussian-noise model. The guide carries this model through likelihood, normal equations, and a penalized fit.
refs: Stanford CS229: linear regression and Bayesian regularization

chapters.title: Naïve Bayes: From Word Counts to a Prediction
chapters.description: Classify a message from four visible training examples, with smoothing, log scores, Gaussian inputs, and linear boundaries.
chapters.alt: Original handwritten page deriving conditional independence and a product of class-conditional feature probabilities.
chapters.caption: Naïve bayes.pdf, page 3: conditional independence and class scoring. The four-message example adds explicit counts and a normalized prediction.
refs: scikit-learn: Naïve Bayes models and smoothing

chapters.title: Logistic Regression: From Scores to Learning
chapters.description: Calculate sigmoid probabilities, cross-entropy, gradients and one update, then connect regularization to MAP.
chapters.alt: Original handwritten chain-rule derivation of logistic regression gradients and their matrix shapes.
chapters.caption: Logistic Regression.pdf, page 3: the gradient derivation. The table above supplies the prediction-minus-label terms and an actual update.
refs: Stanford CS229: logistic regression and regularization

chapters.title: K-means: Build and Check the Clusters
chapters.description: Trace six points through K-means, then calculate WCSS, silhouette, Dunn index, and K-means++ sampling probabilities.
chapters.alt: Original handwritten formulas for within-cluster sum of squares and the silhouette score, with definitions of average distances.
chapters.caption: Clustering.pdf, page 2: WCSS and silhouette. The six-point example makes the squared-distance and ordinary-distance calculations explicit.

chapters.title: PCA and LDA: Choose What a Projection Preserves
chapters.description: Compute PCA variance and reconstruction, then complete the original ten-point Fisher LDA example.
chapters.alt: Original handwritten Fisher criterion, projected class means and within-class scatter derivation.
chapters.caption: PCA and LDA.pdf, page 3: Fisher’s separation-to-scatter criterion. The numerical LDA example transcribes the data from page 4 of the same PDF.
